EV-EVSE Assignment EVSE assignment is done using a heuristic rule based on the EV’s arrival SOC. If the EV SOC is greater than 40% at arrival, it is assigned to a 25-kW charger. Otherwise, if the SOC is lower than 40%, which typically entails a longer charging time, the EV is assigned to a high-power 350-kW charger. This assignment is made in the context of RCCs, which have distinct areas for quick turnaround where fast charging is expected to be employed, and longer-term storage areas where slow charging will be more prevalent. EVSE Curtailment EVSE power curtailment is done using a proportional approach, which reduces the power of all EVSE currently operating in the same proportion. One key factor is that the Gold SCM standard does not assume knowledge of the EV’s charge acceptance curve, which makes it challenging to estimate the EV’s maximum power consumption. While an iterative control algorithm could be used to estimate the maximum power—for instance, by increasing the power set points slowly over time and identifying the point where it stops changing—it was deemed out of scope for this effort.
